questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: A 32 year female patient come to the emergency and was diagnosed with a bleeding gastric ulcer. The best drug to use in this situation is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pantoprazole

Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Pantoprazole is used to treat erosive esophagitis (damage to the esophagus from stomach acid caused by gastroesophageal reflux disease, or GERD) in adults and children who are at least 5 years old



Lange Katzung, Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 1092

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: A patient had GERD and was prescribed omeprazole. He took the drug for 2 years on his own without consulting the doctor again. The following problems may be seen in this patient except for?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypogastrinemia
  • Gastrin is a peptide hormone that stimulates the secretion of gastric acid (HCl) by the parietal cells of the stomach and aids in gastric motility. It is released by G cells in the pyloric antrum of the stomach, duodenum, and pancreas.
  • Gastrin binds to cholecystokinin B receptors to stimulate the release of histamines in enterochromaffin-like cells.
    • Decreases the absorption of vitamin b12 due to decreased activity of intrinsic factor
    • Increased risk of bone fracture due to impaired Ca2+ absorption from intestine
    • Increased susceptibility to certain infections (e.g., hospital-acquired pneumonia, community-acquired clostridium difficile, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in patients with ascites)
    • Hypergastrinemia


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 912

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: PPI was prescribed for gastric ulcer patients. He was advised to take it half an hour before meals and the main Reason for this is?

options.label: A
options.text: Concurrent administration of food may reduce somewhat the rate of absorption of proton pump inhibitors

options.label: B
options.text: Proton pumps are highly active half a before food

options.label: C
options.text: Because an acidic pH in the parietal cell acid canaliculi is required for drug activation and food stimulates acid production

options.label: D
options.text: Before food, p H of the intestine will be alkaline making it easier for absorption of PPI

questions.answerText: Because an acidic pH in the parietal cell acid canaliculi is required for drug activation and food stimulates acid production
questions.solutionHtml:
Because an acidic pH in the parietal cell acid canaliculi is required for drug activation and food stimulates acid production

Because an acidic pH in the parietal cell acid canaliculi is required for drug activation and food stimulates acid production, these drugs ideally should be given about 30 min before meals and also food activates proton pumps and these pumps are inactivated by PPIs



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 910

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: Pirenzepine is an M1 receptor antagonist and it is used in?
questions.solutionHtml:
Peptic ulcer

Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is a break in the inner lining of the stomach, the first part of the small intestine, or sometimes the lower esophagus. An ulcer in the stomach is called a gastric ulcer, while one in the first part of the intestines is a duodenal ulcer. The most common symptoms of a duodenal ulcer are waking at night with upper abdominal pain and upper abdominal pain that improves with eating. With a gastric ulcer, the pain may worsen with eating.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 702

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: Sucralfate was advised for patients with gastric ulcers for ulcer healing. One of the following comorbid diseases this drug should be avoided:
questions.solutionHtml:
Renal failure
  • Sucralfate consists of the octal sulfate of sucrose to which aluminum hydroxide has been added
  • Sucralfate should be avoided in patients with renal failure because some aluminum can be absorbed who are at risk for aluminum overload.
  • Small amount of Aluminium that is absorbed is excreted by the kidney. This is impaired in renal failure leading to aluminum toxicity, which may present with encephalopathy, or osteoporosis


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 913

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: A Pregnant lady at 30 weeks gestation has peptic ulcer disease. All the following drugs can be used except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Misoprostol

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus. It is taken by mouth when used to prevent gastric ulcers in people taking NSAIDs.



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 12th Edition, Page Number: 1315

questions.stem: A 45-year female was having abdominal pain after food and she has advised endoscopy. On endoscopy, she had a gastric ulcer, and a biopsy specimen was sent for H. pylori and was positive for it. All of the following antibiotics have been used in the treatment of H. Pylori infection, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ciprofloxacin

Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic, used in the treatment of bacterial infections. It is also used in treating infections of the urinary tract, nose, throat, skin and soft tissues, and lungs (pneumonia). It prevents the bacterial cells from dividing and repairing, thereby killing them



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 917

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: A patient presents with severe abdominal pain. Endoscopy reveals several benign ulcers in the antral mucosa of the stomach. When therapy is started, which will provide the fastest relief of the discomfort with just a single dose?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antacids
  • The typical symptoms of the acid-peptic disease are caused by acid.
  • Although antacids seem to have no ability to accelerate ulcer healing,
  • They act almost instantaneously to neutralize acid (provided adequate dosages are given), thereby relieving pain and other discomforts that are due to the acid in a matter of a minute or so.
  • All the other drugs can, to varying degrees, suppress gastric acid secretion and ultimately get the patient near or to a “no acid, no pain” state. However, it takes some time (variable, but clearly longer than it takes for an antacid to work) for other medications to be absorbed and reach blood levels sufficient to suppress acid production and then reduce symptoms.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 703

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: Which of the following is wrong about proton pump inhibitors?
questions.solutionHtml:
Short-acting

Proton pump inhibitors are long-acting sulphonamide derivatives. These act by blocking the enzyme Na+K+ ATPase. The drugs are well absorbed orally and in the apex of parietal canaliculi; these drugs get converted into their active moiety.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 697

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: A patient with peptic ulcer was prescribed ranitidine and sucralfate in the morning hours. Why is this combination incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Ranitidine combines with sucralfate and prevents its action

options.label: B
options.text: Combination of these two drugs produces serious side effects like agranulocytosis

options.label: C
options.text: Ranitidine increases the gastric pH so sucralfate is not able to act.

options.label: D
options.text: Sucralfate inhibits the absorption of ranitidine

questions.answerText: Ranitidine increases the gastric pH so sucralfate is not able to act.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ranitidine increases the gastric pH so sucralfate is not able to act.

  • Sucralfate is an ulcer protective agent. It forms a coating over the ulcer base after polymerization.
  • Sucralfate polymerizes only at acidic pH < 4). Ranitidine is an H2 blocker that reduces gastric acid secretion. If both of these drugs are combined, the action of sucralfate will be abolished due to the rise in pH by ranitidine.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 704

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs For Peptic Ulcer Disease
questions.stem: Choose the Correct statement about H2 receptor blockers:

options.label: A
options.text: They are the most efficacious drugs in inhibiting gastric acid secretion

options.label: B
options.text: They cause faster healing of duodenal ulcers

options.label: C
options.text: They prevent stress ulcers in the stomach

options.label: D
options.text: They afford the most prompt relief of ulcer pain

questions.answerText: They prevent stress ulcers in the stomach
questions.solutionHtml:
They prevent stress ulcers in the stomach
  • H2 receptor blockers like ranitidine are used to prevent stress ulcers.H2 blockers are seldom used now to heal peptic ulcers, because PPIs are faster acting, produce more complete pain relief, heal a larger percentage of ulcers in a shorter time.
  • Intravenous infusion of H2 blockers successfully prevents the gastric lesions and hemorrhage as well as promotes healing of erosions that have occurred


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 699
